title: Solvent mixtures for flow batteries found through an AI–experiment cycle
summary: PNNL and Argonne identified solvent mixtures that dissolve three times more than a compound proposed for flow batteries, exploring less than 10% of about 2,000 combinations. The model receives experimental data and guides subsequent experiments; the result concerns solubility, without demonstrating performance of a complete battery.
ai_technology: Machine learning in a loop with high-throughput experiments
organization: Pacific Northwest National Laboratory and Argonne National Laboratory

evidence.tested: Active learning guided solubility measurements of 2,1,3-benzothiadiazole in binary solvents: 218 measurements from 2,101 candidates found 18 mixtures above 6.20 M; best 6.50 M. On a 98-solvent set, Bayesian optimization needed 17 ± 11 trials versus about 50 ± 27 random.
evidence.unknown: Tested one solute, binary solvents only; solubility is not the only property and viscosity, conductivity and stability were not optimized. Model accuracy on 40 test solvents was R2 = 0.63. Real battery performance not reported.
evidence.ai_role: A Gaussian process model with an expected-improvement rule chose which solvents to measure; a robotic platform prepared samples and NMR measured solubility; humans selected features and candidate lists.
